target_customer: Indian households buying a low price smart home camera, with restaurants, factories and dealerships named as later targets
problem: Home cameras stream raw video to the cloud with little intelligence, so owners get constant false alerts and privacy worries.
business_model: Hardware sales through Amazon and Flipkart plus an AI subscription (one year bundled)

founders.name: Sourav Sanyal
previous_startups: Small entertainment company for teens (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; now building OurEye, a B2B SaaS product. CEO title from Crunchbase and 100X.VC coverage.

founders.name: Miran Junaidi
founders.background_notes: Listed under Former Founders on the YC page; no career details given.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to design custom battery powered camera hardware, edge AI for face and motion recognition, a mobile app and cloud storage, and ship at a very low price.

defensibility.rationale: Cheap smart cameras from established Indian and Chinese brands were already on Amazon India and compete on price; face recognition and WhatsApp alerts are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Counterpoint reports these brands dominating Indian smart camera shipments in 2022 and 2023 (Tapo 17 percent share in 2022, CP Plus 45 percent in Q1 2023), with AvairSense absent from the lists.

market_need_then: Counterpoint reported Indian smart home security camera shipments growing 76 percent in 2022, so demand was rising, but most sales were below INR 3,000.

branding.domain_note: avairsense.com; earlier brand OurEye.ai used a .ai domain.

identity.visual_style: Product page focused on Sense 1 specs

rebrands.why: Not stated; CB Insights notes the former name and the YC listing uses AvairSense.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, and the name is easily confused with Awair air quality monitors and Avair companies in search results.

outcome_analysis: The cause of AvairSense's inactive status is not public; no shutdown announcement or post-mortem was found and the product page was still live. The company raised small amounts (about $650K reported) for a hardware product in a price-driven Indian market led by CP Plus, Xiaomi, Tapo and Qubo, but no source states why it stopped, so no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Competitor list left empty: searches found no sources dated near early 2022 that name rivals; market share figures (CP Plus, Xiaomi, Tapo, Qubo) are from 2022 and 2023 Counterpoint reports and are used only in takeover_risk_then. The 2022-02-07 convertible note ($0.5M, total $650K) rests on CB Insights alone. The 2020 round conflicts across outlets: YourStory says $120K from angels including 100X.VC and Amara Ventures (Dec 2020); Indian Startup News describes a $35K pre-seed and a $150K seed in Aug 2020. The IPVM post about a shut down Andy Rubin backed camera startup was not tied to AvairSense. The YC page lists the founders as former founders; Dealroom shows $654K over three rounds.
